Name: Matt Loomis
Badge: Joining a Conversation
What is one insight you gained from completing the Atwoodian Table yourself that might shape how you introduce it to students?:

Note-taking symbols make it possible.

How does the Atwoodian Table idea compare to how you have taught argument and/or responding to multiple texts in the past?:
The Atwoodian Table is an improvement in spatial arrangement and the inclusion student viewpoint/perspective in the planning stage.
What do you notice about the two sets of excerpts in this module (children in fancy restaurants and toddlers and technology)? How do the excerpts work together to invite students to join the conversation? What are some conversations related to topics you teach?:
In each set, the excerpts cover common ground within the topics - main ideas, key details, statement of position, recommendations, etc. This focuses attention on elements that are easy to compare/contrast with minimal reading. Historical debates lend themselves to conversations of this type (Who fired first at the Battle of Lexington? What caused the Civil War?).
